summary: Five-part series on how crack spread through US inner cities in the 1980s, the CIA-backed Contras' cocaine trafficking and the Iran-Contra affair, the racist moral panic and sentencing laws that followed, and the discrediting of journalist Gary Webb.

evidence.note: crack enters US inner cities around 1981, starting in southern California
crack-baby moral panic begins with a small medical study amplified by the press
100-to-1 crack sentencing rule and racial incarceration disparities
Webb publishes Dark Alliance in August 1996
Nicaraguan history: Somoza dictatorship and Sandinista revolution
part three covers the Iran side of Iran-Contra
North turns to Panama's Noriega to fund the Contras
press shuts down questions about Contra drug trafficking

notes: Parts 3-4 are Hood Politics episodes (crossover), but formats.yaml lists Cracktoberfest as a deep-dive example, so deep-dive. No person primary, so roles empty. Only 2,000-word excerpts for parts 2-5: CIA heroin program (likely Laos) and Iran backstory start years are unverified, so covered_span start is a guess. Webb's 2004 death assumed covered in part 5.
